title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models

details.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
details.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. Diffusion drafters such as DFlash propose an entire token block in a single forward pass, but mainly focus on text-only tasks, leaving multimodal drafting underexplored. To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input. We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training. Motivated by this observation, we propose MMFlash, a simple and effective framework that adaptively upweights visually dependent tokens that the drafter predicts poorly. For long video inputs, MMFlash further employs sparse attention to reduce redundant attention computation and improve drafting quality. Across various multimodal benchmarks, MMFlash achieves lossless decoding speedups of up to 3.58×, outperforming EAGLE-3 and DFlash by up to 195.4% and 17.1%, respectively.

title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding

details.title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
details.abstract: • We analyze the relationship between entropy spike steps and hallucinations in multimodal diffusion models from the perspective of uncertainty dynamics across denoising steps. • We propose StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding approach that mitigates hallucinations through entropy spike detection and step-aware mode switching. • Extensive evaluations across four MDLM backbones and diverse multimodal benchmarks show the superior performance of StepRefine, offering an effective solution for multimodal diffusion hallucinations.

Leads every size class on 11 video benchmarks (4B: 72.14 avg), strongest on dynamics (TOMATO, Vinoground, SSv2) Beats Meta's V-JEPA 2 / 2.1 video LLMs with 1/20 of the training data and 1/9 of the visual tokens 4.53M public samples, 32 visual tokens per frame, one training stage All 6 checkpoints, code and a live demo are open.

title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL

details.title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL

For example, this month’s revenue report by region can use the same joins and revenue calculation as last month’s, with only the date range changing. We built HARE to benchmark this kind of reuse and MEM-SQL to carry it out using verified query history.

title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple

details.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
details.abstract: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

title: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers

details.title: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers
details.abstract: In this paper, we study how residual connections should retain and reuse information when the same Transformer blocks run repeatedly. Inspired by recurrent memory, we develop a unified view of residual connections as memory operating along network depth . The write–transport–read formulation lets us compare different residual designs through what they store, how they carry information forward, and how they retrieve it for subsequent computation. Guided by this view, we introduce Loopback Transformer . Loopback stores individual block updates, uses geometric forgetting to progressively discount earlier passes, and learns content-dependent attention over the stored updates. This allows the model to retrieve useful information from earlier computation. At matched training tokens and executed depth, Loopback achieves lower validation loss and higher mean accuracy across 13 zero-shot tasks than Standard Transformers at both 1.4B and 3B, retaining only 68% and 75% of their Transformer parameters , respectively. At 3B, validation loss improves from 2.0005 to 1.9849 , mean accuracy rises from 48.56% to 49.45% , and Loopback scores higher on 11 of 13 tasks . In our main comparisons at 191M, 374M, and 778M, it also achieves the lowest validation loss and highest thirteen-task mean among Standard and seven looped residual baselines. Parameter counts exclude token embeddings and the output head. Our results highlight residual design as an important part of parameter-efficient modeling: sharing computation works better when the model also learns how to retain and reuse its outputs. We welcome feedback and discussion!

title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents

details.title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
details.abstract: What happens when an AI agent decides to improve itself? More importantly, how do we know whether those improvements are actually making it better? As agents begin modifying their own prompts, memories, tools, and workflows, one question becomes increasingly important: Should every self-generated improvement be trusted? This paper introduces Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for ensuring that an agent's proposed improvements earn the right to become permanent through independent evaluation, measurable evidence, and safeguards against capability degradation. The central idea is simple: An AI agent should be free to propose changes, but evidence should decide which changes survive. I'd be interested to hear your thoughts on how we should govern the next generation of self-evolving AI agents.

title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions

details.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
details.abstract: Bonbon is a vertical foundation model for biology that independently learned the hidden relationships governing molecular interactions, just as LLMs learned math without being explicitly trained on it. Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 main track as an Oral (top 0.4% of submissions). Trained on sequences alone, with no structure, physics, task-specific labels, or supervision, Bonbon developed emergent biological capabilities as we scaled it from 42M to 1.6B parameters. Pretraining loss fell smoothly, while new capabilities appeared sharply at the largest scale: What it does: predicts mechanism of action across six classes, including which molecules switch the same target on and which switch it off. Today this requires functional lab assays. Where it happens: localizes the binding site and distinguishes orthosteric from allosteric engagement on the same target. How it bonds: recognizes covalent binding and pinpoints the residue involved, without being told covalency is present. Which atoms matter: identifies the active moiety at single-bond resolution, work that usually takes many rounds of making and testing analogs. All capabilities were evaluated zero-shot on held-out proteins and molecules. The same representation space reaches state-of-the-art performance on widely used binding and affinity benchmarks, and runs at 2,500 molecular interactions per second on a single H100, about 50,000× faster than a leading co-folding model. In blinded dose-response assays at an external CRO, de novo molecules ranked by Bonbon achieved a 61.5% hit rate across nine disease targets in seven protein families, compared with the ~0.1% typical of high-throughput screening. Every molecule was less than 60% similar to anything in training. Some examples: HDAC6: most known inhibitors rely on hydroxamate chemistry linked to toxicity. Bonbon found novel non-hydroxamate inhibitors. MNK2: novel inhibitors outside the documented chemical space for this cancer target. VEGFR2 and ELANE: both absent from training, yet Bonbon found confirmed inhibitors for each. Why it matters Most AI in drug discovery answers one narrow question: does a molecule fit a protein? But a molecule can fit perfectly and still do nothing, or the opposite of what you need. What it does, where it acts, how it holds, and which atoms drive it are usually answered through a long chain of separate assays and lab iterations. Bonbon answers these questions together, in a single inference pass, at the scale biology demands. That collapses months of sequential experiments into one step, opens chemistry beyond known scaffolds, and puts the hardest drug programs within reach, including targets with no good starting points. More broadly, it shows that the rules of molecular biology are learnable from sequence alone and emerge with scale. That is the foundation for moving from single interactions to pathways, cells, and understanding biology as a complex system.

title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation

details.title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation
details.abstract: What if you could teach a mobile robot by walking with it and guiding its grippers by hand? HALO collects demonstrations up to 2.9× faster. The learned policies grasp and steer a chair precisely while staying in motion, pull apart tightly fitted LEGO pieces in different configurations, guide a tiny zip-tie tip through its locking head, and coordinate both arms and the moving base to pack boxes quickly on a conveyor line, cycle after cycle.

title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device

details.title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device
details.abstract: In this paper, we ask whether a specialized language model can be built automatically for a given task and a given phone. Mobile AI Factory is an agentic system that fine-tunes and quantizes small language models, and uses real measurements of the target phone to choose the model, precision, inference engine and backend. Across ten tasks and four Android phones, its on-device models outperform or match five-shot frontier models on eight tasks, and the best configuration changes from phone to phone. Code is available at https://github.com/evanly-gh/SLM_Factory

title: eDIAR: Training-Free Open-Speaker Streaming Diarization for Long Meetings and Large Archives via e-means

details.title: eDIAR: Training-Free Open-Speaker Streaming Diarization for Long Meetings and Large Archives via e-means
details.abstract: We take the speaker embeddings from each slot (WeSpeaker ResNet34) and split them using Meta's recently released e-means. For streaming, each chunk reclusters only the most recent 90-second window and allows label corrections only within the last 10 seconds. This keeps the computational cost constant regardless of meeting length, at about 57 ms per update. The results: With 20 speakers, DER drops from 66.5% to 43.7%, a relative reduction of about 34%. At the 45-minute mark of one-hour meetings with 12–20 speakers, Streaming Sortformer reaches around 57% DER, while our method stays around 25%. When e-means is used for frame-level speaker association, matching the same speaker across recordings with 1,251 speakers is several times faster than with Lloyd's k-means.

title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving

details.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
details.abstract: TL;DR: Removing GPS from vehicle logs does not protect location privacy: we introduce CANTraj (3,940 naturalistic drives paired with GNSS trajectories) and CANTraj-Bench (1,380 hours, 85,919 km) to benchmark six re-implemented route-inference attacks and new baselines under unified protocols, showing that combining CAN steering signals with road-network constraints recovers 87%–88% of 5-minute routes with a median error of just 37–43 m—even under signal quantization.

title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix

details.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
details.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. In contrast, we find that humans draw only 8.4% of their weaknesses from the appendix, and these weaknesses primarily revolve around a paper’s presentation and content related to its core idea. Meanwhile, LLMs draw weaknesses from deep in the appendix that concern fine-grained technical details not central to the paper’s contributions. We anticipate that our analysis will contribute to the scholarly discourse on AI reviews.

title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift

details.title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift
details.abstract: We test whether 73 no-reference image quality metrics agree with what people prefer on underwater photos. Using four opinion-score sets and our own paired-comparison study (20 raters, 1,920 choices), we find that agreement with human choices is low. Simple edits such as saturation, sharpening and CLAHE raise the scores of popular underwater metrics, and repeated generative edits with Nano Banana drift away from the scene while some metrics still reward them. Code and all scores are public on GitHub and Hugging Face.

title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams

details.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
details.abstract: JFinBench is a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from six certification exams held in 2026. Building benchmarks from public exam PDFs is challenging due to heterogeneous layouts, complex tables and figures, and diverse question formats. We address this with a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline: a vision-language model converts PDFs into layout-preserving Markdown, a coding agent generates exam-specific conversion code and review interfaces, and humans verify all examples and provide feedback for corrections. This reduces verification to roughly two hours per exam, enabling practical benchmark updates as new exams are released. Evaluating 12 LLMs, we find that leading proprietary models exceed 93%, outperforming the best open-weight model by 12 percentage points, mainly due to gaps in specialized knowledge. Web and terminal access improves all models and narrows the gap, but a 4-point difference remains, with rankings largely unchanged (Spearman ρ = 0.87). These findings highlight the importance of knowledge encoded in model parameters, even when external tools are available.

title: Disen-Forcing: Disentangling Semantic Anchoring from Motion for Autoregressive Video Diffusion

details.title: Disen-Forcing: Disentangling Semantic Anchoring from Motion for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
details.abstract: The frame sink trick in autoregressive video diffusion models helps keep long-horizon rollouts consistent, but it also pulls motion toward low-dynamic modes. We find that long-range consistency is carried by a small subset of attention heads, while most heads handle local temporal dynamics. Disen-Forcing is a distillation-time plug-in that routes the frame sink context only to those anchoring heads and regularizes motion to be invariant to the frame sink, so long-horizon consistency and motion dynamics both improve.

The benchmark supports multiple harness integrations, including BrowserGym and Harbor for running MCP and coding agents.

title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery

details.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
details.abstract: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world’s energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. Urban Building Energy Modelling (UBEM) is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing UBEM is largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce and limited; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal generative AI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consumption maps. We decouple long-term static urban morphology from short-term dynamic energy consumption. By conditioning on static urban land use, DySENSE can generate realistic, diverse and new static urban imagery with aligned energy maps. By conditioning on dynamic monthly and climate prompts, DySENSE can jointly generate dynamic, monthly energy consumption maps while keeping the urban morphology static. Experiments across four cities (New York City, Washington, D.C., Norfolk, and Busan) demonstrated that DySENSE can generate annotated high-fidelity synthetic energy data using less than 25% labelled data, boosting downstream prediction performance by 8% mIoU, and achieving strong energy dynamic consistency. Compared to existing energy prediction methods, DySENSE significantly improved prediction performance (about 8.7% accuracy) and reduced prediction error (9%-18% CVRMSE, ASHRAE metrics). DySENSE offers an effective foundation to support energy-efficient urban planning, peak-load analysis, building performance simulation and dynamic demand response for urban, energy, and building science.

title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime

details.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
details.abstract: We built Continual-ARC to see whether agents get better with experience, scoring notes in a harness and updates to the weights on the same scale. ARC tasks recur through a stream of 200 instances, each time with a fresh input, and every demonstration or wrong answer costs the learner part of a fixed budget. After the stream we freeze the learner and test it on new instances of the tasks it met (memorization) and on 100 tasks it never met (generalization). Out of the box, most harnesses didn't learn measurably, and most of the harness-based methods we tried learned less than a baseline that just caches each task's demonstrations. Told explicitly to save a verified program per task, all three harnesses we ran on GPT-6 Luna memorized, but they gained little or nothing on unseen tasks. Training the weights did generalize: Qwen3.5-9B, trained with DAgger to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash, spent 29% less than its untrained self on the 100 unseen tasks. Caveat: it's one domain, and most of our runs use fairly small models. Would love to hear where you think the benchmark falls short!

title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare

details.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
details.abstract: InclusionMed is an open evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. Through successive releases of the Atlas and Index, this open collaboration aims to ensure that the diverse healthcare needs of people worldwide guide how progress in medical AI is defined and measured. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks along two axes: healthcare role and AI capability. The role axis distinguishes patients and the public, healthcare professionals, and healthcare administration professionals; the capability axis distinguishes knowledge, reasoning, and agency. The Atlas design makes clear which healthcare needs are represented by the included benchmarks and where coverage remains limited. The InclusionMed Index aggregates model results across the benchmarks included in the Atlas. In the initial release, each model's Index score is the equally weighted mean of its five benchmark scores. The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, revealing differences in both model rankings and score levels.

title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models

details.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
details.abstract: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2× without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/ .

title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection

details.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
details.abstract: Keep your LLM and AI agents. Add SPILLWAY. SPILLWAY 1.0.0, a real-time safety guard for AI agents, is the only one of seven prompt-injection defenses on AgentDojo with zero in-scope attack success in all 12 backbone-by-suite cells, and it has the highest mean utility under attack, 48.9% (next best 45.3%). It checks every tool call before it runs. An instruction hidden in an email or a web page can tell an agent to send your files or money to an attacker. SPILLWAY admits an action's recipient, account or URL when it appears in the user's request or in a typed field that a read-only tool returned, such as an email's sender. An address found only in free text, such as an email body, is refused unless the request delegates it. This check is a set lookup with no model call. An optional local judge may restore a refused call, never one whose target came from injected text the sanitizer removed. Standard attack, 3 backbones x 4 suites, judge on: 0 of 2,847 in-scope attack successes. Every other defense leaks in 3 to 12 of the 12 cells (ROPE 3, DRIFT 7, MELON 10, PI detector 10, Progent 11, Spotlighting 12). Mean utility is 53.9% without attack and 48.9% under attack, compared with DRIFT's 45.3%, ROPE's 34.5% and MELON's 31.4% under attack. Stronger attacks: zero under ChatInject's forged chat template (0 of 665), AutoDojo (0 of 389) and an attacker who sends the injected email (0 of 126). Under PISmith's released RL attacker (gpt-4o-mini, four suites, ASR@1), 0.5% mean in-scope attack success (4 of 949) at 25.7% utility. Against a frontier router: on 7 suites from AgentDojo and AgentDyn (gpt-4o-mini agent), SPILLWAY keeps zero in-scope attack success and more utility than ROPE on every suite, with ROPE routing through its authors' Claude Opus 4.8. ROPE leaks on 3. Cost: the optional judge, a local 4-bit Gemma 4 31B, checks selected calls. On benign qwen3:8b Workspace and Slack episodes, SPILLWAY adds 0.19 to 0.39 model calls per episode, judge included, 13 to 50 times fewer than MELON, Progent and DRIFT. It adds at most 500 ms per task on average compared with the undefended agent, against 1,600 to 10,500 ms for those three. No defense step re-runs the backbone. SPILLWAY's AgentDojo results use the code released as spillway-guard 1.0.0. The comparison defenses, the AgentDyn portion of the router comparison and the cost study retain their original measurements. Connect it where your tools run. The repository has recipes for LangChain and LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, any MCP host and Claude Code hooks. In the recorded Slack episode on the project page, SPILLWAY is the only one of eight runs that posts the reply the user asked for without sending the injected link. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07222 Code and per-cell records: https://github.com/saintmachines/spillway Project page and recorded example: https://saintmachines.github.io/spillway/ Install: pip install -U spillway-guard Author here, happy to answer questions.

title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations

details.title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
details.abstract: A coding agent working within a software organization must establish what to build, collaborate with colleagues, and verify what it delivers. We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains. Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues who have distinct responsibilities, bounded knowledge, and controlled collaboration behavior. Starting from a brief handoff, agents must recover requirements distributed across colleagues and workplace records, reconcile conflicting evidence, and implement changes evaluated by private executable tests. We evaluate eleven models and find a substantial gap between partial implementation and complete task delivery. The two leading models satisfy approximately 63% of fail-to-pass (F2P) tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments. Providing complete requirements upfront improves F2P by approximately 16 percentage points for Seed Evolving and GPT-6 Astra, yet leaves complete task success unchanged. Requirement-level trajectory analysis reveals failures throughout the delivery process: Claude-Opus-5.5 directs a mean of 93% of first questions about queried cards to their accountable owners across runs but obtains only 64% of colleague-held requirements. Deferred questions go unfollowed, implementations remain incomplete even after requirements are acquired, and 31% of requirements reported as completed fail their tests.

title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers

details.title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
details.abstract: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative. However, simply imitating human reviewing is problematic because reviewing serves multiple purposes, including evaluating papers' soundness, interestingness, and clarity, the last two of which are subjective. In this work, we focus solely on evaluating soundness, the most important and objective criterion, and define the learning objective as jointly maximizing (1) precision, based on the soundness and substantiveness of review points, and (2) recall, the coverage of high-quality reference review points. Under this problem formulation, we construct a quality-labeled review point dataset, PaperSound-23K, using 1K ICLR submissions and 23K human-written and LLM-generated review points. Using this dataset, we train an AI reviewer model, PaperCritic, through reinforcement learning with the F1 score of precision and recall as the reward. Our experiments show that PaperCritic outperforms frontier models and models trained with other AI reviewer training methods on an in-domain test set. Surprisingly, learning to review ICLR submissions also transfers to reviewing Nature-family papers and even to out-of-domain reviewing tasks (e.g., code review, legal contract review, and feedback on story writing).

details.title: VoxMel TTS Technical Report

title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization

details.title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
details.abstract: Hi Hugging Face community! We’re introducing Accelerate Bench , a benchmark for evaluating coding agents on application-level program optimization . 🧪 32 scientific workloads across 8 application areas Agents optimize complete CPU applications, including GROMACS, OpenFOAM, and Quantum ESPRESSO. Each task provides a working program, a fixed workload, correctness requirements, and a compute budget. Agents have eight hours to decide where and how to optimize. ✅ Performance gains must preserve correctness Public tests support iterative development. title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos

details.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
details.abstract: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

details.abstract: Can a vision-language model look at a still image of a chain reaction and tell who gets hit? DominoBench tests exactly that: 854 simulator-labelled scenes in minimal pairs, where one quantity moves one grid  step and one person's fate flips. What I found across 30 models: Unaided, no model is reliable. The best are right about the person whose fate flips in at most 75% of items, and get both twins of a pair right in at most 40%. Pointing at the deciding step helps little. Writing out the calculation helps a lot: the same models reach 80–92%. Two families behave very differently. The GPT-6 models are the most accurate unaided but barely gain from the calculation, while GPT-5.6-Sol starts low and ends first. title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers

details.title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
details.abstract: Looped Transformers improve parameter effi- ciency by repeatedly applying the same Trans- former layers. During autoregressive decoding, however, generating each token requires several sequential passes through these layers, leading to high decoding latency. Pipelined self-speculative methods use shallow-loop predictions to process tokens at different loops in the same batch, but each token must reach the drafting depth before the next can enter the pipeline. We introduce LoopFill, a training-free speculative decoding al- gorithm for looped LLM that combines multi- token suffix drafts with shallow-loop predictions in a single draft tree. Both drafters contribute to one tree, so a suffix lookup can immediately extend a shallow prediction and several future to- kens can enter the pipeline together. The shared block computes the highest-scoring draft candi- dates at different loop depths in one batch, and full-depth verification preserves the model’s au- toregressive output distribution. Across seven benchmarks, LoopFill’s average speedup over greedy autoregressive decoding is 5.85×on Ouro- 2.6B and 5.13×on Huginn-3.5B. The speedups exceed those of LoopAhead, the strongest base- line, by 40% on Ouro-2.6B and 25% on Huginn- 3.5B.

details.abstract: 🚀 Excited to introduce GlyphAtlas, a scene text synthesis model built on FLUX.1-Fill-dev—fully open-sourced with code, weights, and a 1.5M dataset! ⚠️ Why existing methods struggle: Standard approaches rely on a scene-aligned glyph image to specify both layout and character shape. Because glyph resolution is tied to region size, small text, dense multi-line layouts, and complex scripts get squeezed into a handful of pixels, resulting in missing, merged, or distorted strokes. 🧠 Our approach: GlyphAtlas decouples where text goes from how strokes are drawn. A scene-aligned glyph image anchors layout, while a resolution-independent glyph atlas—encoded directly via the backbone's native VAE without extra encoders—supplies crisp stroke references. Atlas-anchored attention then binds each cell back to its target region for accurate coarse-to-fine synthesis. 🌍 Zero-shot & Open Source: Trained solely on Chinese and English, GlyphAtlas-Bi generalizes zero-shot to Japanese, Korean, and Arabic, handling everything from curved storefronts and posters to dense book covers. Alongside our code and weights, we also release GlyphAtlas-Data-1.5M (1.5 million scene text images) to support the community! 🌐 Project page: https://fr0zencrane.github.io/project-glyphatlas/ 🤗 Model checkpoint: https://huggingface.co/Fr0zencr4nE/GlyphAtlas 📚 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Fr0zencr4nE/GlyphAtlas-Data-1.5M 💻 Code: https://github.com/Fr0zenCrane/GlyphAtlas Try it out and let us know what you think, feedback and questions are very welcome! 🙌

title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models

details.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 Excited to share ForceHarness , an agent harness that lets frozen API frontier models understand and use wrist force for contact-rich manipulation—with zero demonstrations and zero finetuning . Why ForceHarness? Frontier models can control robots zero-shot from images, yet cameras cannot see contact forces (whether a USB plug has seated, whether a screw thread caught, which bottle is heavier, or whether a door is locked vs. merely stiff). Meanwhile, contact evolves far faster than an API call, and frozen models cannot interpret raw force streams. ForceHarness bridges this gap with two layers: Self-terminating force primitives close the fast force loop beneath the model ( search , wiggle , screw , slide , lift , ...) and stop automatically on contact events while holding safely as the model thinks. Physics translation layer converts each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty (mass, friction, stiffness, contact height, insertion advance)—with no hardcoded task thresholds. Key Highlights 3.3% → 90.0% zero-shot on a real Franka FR3 (no wrist F/T sensor) : Across 6 contact-rich tasks (USB insertion, screw driving, eggplant peeling, whiteboard wiping, bottle weight sorting, and firmness probing) using joint torques alone. Surpasses trained force-aware VLAs (200 demos/task) : Beats $\pi_{0.5}$, ForceVLA, and Diffusion Policy on both ForceBench (82.5% held-out vs. 35.3% best trained) and HiddenPhys , our new 7-task MuJoCo hidden-physics benchmark ( 96.4% / 135/140 , matching expert force controllers with 0 damaged handles ). Drop-in Agent Skill ( SKILL.md ) : Give the repo to your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) and it will check force sensing capability, calibrate, and bring up your simulator or real robot arm gate by gate—never moving hardware without your confirmation. Links 🌐 Project Page & Videos : https://showlab.github.io/ForceHarness/ 💻 Code & Agent Setup Skill : https://github.com/showlab/ForceHarness 📊 HiddenPhys Dataset (1,423 expert demos, raw + LeRobot) : https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jack97/ForceHarness-Data Happy to answer any questions or hear your feedback!

title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement

details.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
details.abstract: Author affiliations (as listed in the paper): Google Cloud AI · Google DeepMind · Google Cloud AI Research · The Pennsylvania State University. We started with a practical question: after spending many rounds improving an agent’s harness, what should we carry forward when the model or benchmark changes? The code is an obvious answer. But it often leaves out why a check was added, what a prompt change was meant to fix, or which earlier attempts failed. That history can matter when the next optimizer has to decide what to keep and what to revise. We study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI) and introduce Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) . SIM groups harness edits by the problems they address and records their rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context. The components proposing and selecting edits both read this history. New attempts extend it as optimization continues, while the task-solving model’s weights stay frozen. Our comparisons start from the same source-evolved harness, with matched target tasks, policy, optimization rounds, and candidate budgets. Across four domains, full SIM achieves higher final scores than harness-only and root-cause-only continuation in the six cross-dataset and four Opus-to-Gemini comparisons we test. We also run ten independent coding source optimizations, each followed by paired continuations with and without SIM. SIM finishes ahead in nine pairs, with a mean gain of 2.36 score points (95% CI: 1.05–3.68; p = 0.003). The setting requires compatible execution interfaces. Most main cross-domain comparisons use one run per condition, and matching rounds does not imply equal token or runtime cost. These results support carrying optimization history into continued search; they do not guarantee improvement on every transfer. The images below show the idea and the coding results, including the negative pair. Happy to discuss the setup or hear how others preserve this kind of experience. 📄 https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18856

title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion

details.title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
details.abstract: π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs. It couples a geometry branch with a geometry-conditioned motion branch, which predicts image-space correspondences that are lifted into 3D using reconstructed target-view geometry. Across diverse benchmarks, π^4 achieves the best overall average rank in geometry evaluation, alongside competitive performance in single- and multiview 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation. With a shared backbone, the full geometry-and-motion system contains approximately 0.5B parameters---less than half the size of most baselines. It produces joint reconstructions and tracks in one forward pass, including large-scale scenes with thousands of input images despite training with contexts of at most 64 views. title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop

details.title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
details.abstract: Coding agents are taking on longer-horizon, more complex development tasks, and training also needs to cover the complete project development process. 🚀 However, existing environment construction pipelines often stop at execution and validation, lacking further optimization of how much training value the task itself can provide and how it can be improved. 🤔 We hope to introduce feedback-driven iteration from recursive self-improvement (RSI) into environment construction, so that tasks continuously increase their training value during the construction process. 🔄 However, related methods often rely on model rollouts or downstream evaluations after model training to judge whether modifications are effective. For long-horizon coding tasks, a single complete solution involves a large amount of implementation and debugging, further increasing computational cost and feedback cycles. ⏳💰 This prompts us to ask: can we avoid relying on high-cost, long-cycle downstream feedback and instead find reliable, low-cost, immediate proxy metrics to guide environment improvement? 🎯 RepoFactory builds complete project development environments from real software repositories and uses the product of reasonableness, implementation scope, and structural coupling as the environment evolution objective. 🏭 Validation execution and code analysis provide timely, low-cost proxy feedback, guiding the agent to jointly modify task instructions, reference implementations, and tests, thereby ensuring environment validity while increasing the implementation work and component collaboration required by the task. 🔍✅ Each round of modification yields new feedback that continues to guide the next iteration, without waiting for a complete rollout of the solving model or downstream training. 🔁 Ultimately, we constructed 10,159 environments covering 17 software domains. 📊 RepoHorizen-35B-A3B, trained on these environments, improves by 22.6 percentage points on NL2Repo-Bench compared with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, and by 8.5 percentage points on average across five benchmarks. 📈 Among these, environment evolution brings an additional gain of 5.1 and 2.1 percentage points on these two metrics, respectively. 🎉 We are releasing an initial batch of 200 non-evolved environments and corresponding Docker images. 🐳📦 Friends working on coding agents, training data, and environment construction are welcome to get in touch. 🤝✨

title: Beyond Answering: Learning to Speak First and Act in Streaming Video

details.title: Beyond Answering: Learning to Speak First and Act in Streaming Video
details.abstract: Hi Hugging Face community! 👋 We’re excited to share AURA 2.0 — Beyond Answering: Learning to Speak First and Act in Streaming Video. What if a video AI could notice something worth discussing and start the conversation, rather than always waiting for a question? AURA 2.0 is an open-source streaming video understanding model that brings together three capabilities: Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC): Decide whether to speak, when to speak, and what to say based on the evolving video and dialogue context—including when to remain silent. Stream-Aware Tool Calling (SATC): Select tools and construct arguments from the current visual context, then incorporate tool results into the conversation. Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG): Connect dialogue to specific objects through user-provided visual cues and model-generated, frame-aligned bounding boxes. The model is trained on approximately 5,400 hours of video and 40 million frames, with three-stage training and long-horizon interaction memory. It achieves the highest reported aggregate scores across IPIBench, StreamArena, ProactiveVideoQA, and PhoStream among the models compared in our report. Explore the demos and find code, model downloads, and deployment instructions on our project page. We welcome feedback, reproductions, and discussion—especially on how proactive video assistants should balance useful intervention with knowing when to wait!

title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns

details.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
details.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and τ2-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces τ2-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises τ2 accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

title: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models

details.title: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
details.abstract: ResWAM is a world-action model for robot manipulation that learns to predict what changes in the scene (the residual), and it uses this change-focused prediction to guide action generation.

title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications

details.title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications
details.abstract: We introduce VisualArtifactSpec 1.0 (VAS) , a benchmark for evaluating agent-authored visual artifacts. VAS includes 211 creation and modification tasks across 4 artifact families: 📊 Presentations: creating decks from scratch, working with templates, and editing existing slides. 🎨 Static graphics: posters, infographics, banners, and multi-image series. 🎬 Animations and videos: animated graphics, animated videos, and video editing. 🌐 Web interfaces: content browsing, data exploration, interactive tools, and workflows. We evaluate two aspects separately: ① Task Fulfillment: Does the artifact satisfy explicit task requirements? ② Artifact Performance: How well do its content, organization, visuals, and delivery serve the intended context? Across nine model–harness configurations, we find that meeting requirements does not necessarily make an artifact suitable for its intended context. For example, science cards may contain all the required information but differ substantially in visual hierarchy and readability on a phone. We welcome feedback on the benchmark, evaluation protocol, and agent results!

title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?

details.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
details.abstract: TL;DR: We give an LLM agent a general self-improvement goal, a budget, and basic tools for collecting experience and editing text. We do not give it real tasks or an explicit recipe. Sufficiently capable models successfully compose their own self-improvement loops using human-recognizable learning strategies.

title: MPEG-Diffusion: Mixed-Resolution Video Generation

details.title: MPEG-Diffusion: Mixed-Resolution Video Generation
details.abstract: MPEG Diffusion for video gen: high-resolution on important subjects, low-res on the background to save compute while keeping visual quality. It features: Close to full-res DiT self-select high-res regions Up to 4.8× faster (30% tokens)

title: Regularized Score Centering

details.title: Regularized Score Centering
details.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update, even without full importance sampling (IS). Our empirical study shows that full IS produces extreme gradients and that SC significantly reduces their magnitude. However, SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback–Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner’s next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy’s next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9× the strongest baseline’s score on BabyAI.

title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback

details.title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
details.abstract: Can a language model program a CNC machine without computing a single coordinate? 🛠️ MillBill turns a B-rep part, its stock and its material into G-code for indexed 3-axis milling. The LLM only makes the machining decisions: operations, tools, cutting parameters. A geometric harness does the geometry: it recognises features, chooses setups by what the cutters can actually reach (not just by visibility), generates every toolpath, simulates material removal and returns per-feature deviations so the model can refine the plan. 📊 On 100 GrabCAD parts, every program is scored by simulation. With the open Qwen3.8-27B running locally, MillBill leaves 97.4% of the target surface within 0.1 mm. The best frontier code-writing agent (GPT-6 Astra) reaches 94.3%, Claude Opus 5.5 83.0% and CNC-Net 42.3%. 📦 Open release: code, plus 4,294 GrabCAD parts paired with milling stocks and a simulator that scores any planner's G-code. 💻 https://github.com/kulibinai/millbill 🤗 https://huggingface.co/datasets/kulibinai/millbill

title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference

details.title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
details.abstract: CADMAGEDDON: mesh → editable CAD with one open-weight model, no frontier API needed 🛠️ Most mesh-to-CAD systems make a model write the whole program, including every coordinate and dimension. We split each feature in two: • geometric instruments detect and name the entities on the target mesh (levels, fitted lines/arcs, faces, hole stacks, patterns) and fit their exact values; • a mid-sized VLM (Qwen3.8-27B) looks at renders and decides only what to build next and what to fix, referring to geometry by name. No reconstruction model is trained. The agent emits CadQuery or native FreeCAD programs, and the model fits on a single 48 GB GPU. Results (vs. the strongest baseline, CADFather): • MCB: IoU 0.862 → 0.933 , GMS 0.705 → 0.818 • CADENA-Bench: GMS 0.800 → 0.909 • BenchCAD (64³ voxel IoU): 0.991 , above the best self-reported frontier entry (0.963) Code: https://github.com/kulibinai/cadmageddon

title: AuXSpec: Learning to Autoformalize Program Specifications via Executable Postconditions

details.title: AuXSpec: Learning to Autoformalize Program Specifications via Executable Postconditions
details.abstract: We introduce AuXSpec, a Lean framework that pairs each declarative postcondition with an executable postcondition, so test cases can check generated specifications by execution. 🔐 This unlocks execution-based reinforcement learning for formal specification generation. 🛠️ Trained on 19.5K SFT samples and then with RL on 13.6K tasks under this execution-based reward, AuXSpec-27B-RL improves SpecGen pass@4 over its base model (AuXSpec-Test 14.3% → 84.3%, out-of-domain Verina 21.9% → 90.5%) and outperforms all frontier models on our 300-problem benchmark AuXSpec-Test. The model also generates the fewest output tokens per response (1.8K vs. 9.7K for Claude-Opus-5). 🤗 Models, data and the benchmark: https://huggingface.co/collections/eth-algopt/auxspec

title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models

details.title: PanDWM: Panoramic 4D Driving World Models
details.abstract: We present PanDWM, a panoramic 4D driving world model that generates view-consistent 360° scenes from multi-camera layouts. Our approach combines a causal generative model with a feed-forward 3D Gaussian decoder for efficient dynamic scene reconstruction. Experiments on nuScenes show improved generation quality and substantially faster inference than multi-camera baselines. We welcome feedback and discussion.

title: The Noise Floor of a Quantization Comparison: Engine, restart, batch and kernel drift, measured against 8-bit and 4-bit effects in two decision models

details.title: The Noise Floor of a Quantization Comparison: Engine, restart, batch and kernel drift, measured against 8-bit and 4-bit effects in two decision models
details.abstract: We measured how much a quantized model's decisions move for reasons that have nothing to do with quantization: a different serving engine, a restart, a different batch size or kernel. On Cloudflare's Clef and Clef-flash, those alone move up to 0.92% of decisions, about what Q8_0 moves (0.88% and 1.04%). 4-bit moves 3.5% to 5.8%. Code, per-record outputs and the pre-registration are on GitHub, and all six quantized builds are in the collection linked above.

title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

details.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
details.abstract: M3OPD-Reasoner is a fully open recipe that post-trains Qwen3.5-9B into one reasoning model for image STEM, image perception and video. 🌐 Project page: https://ngquangtrung57.github.io/m3opd-reasoner-page/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/ngquangtrung57/M3OPD-Reasoner 🤗 Models (all stages): https://huggingface.co/collections/ngqtrung/m3opd-reasoner-6aed5164d151b6643a1b3b2d 📊 SFT data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ngqtrung/M3OPD-SFT-1.35M 📊 RL data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ngqtrung/M3OPD-RL-193K 💬 alphaXiv: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.23034

title: TPHC: Improving Hyper-Connections with Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates

details.title: TPHC: Improving Hyper-Connections with Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates
details.abstract: By aligning HC stream updates with TP shards, TPHC delivers consistent gains over mHC without adding parameters or FLOPs. The three of us, sharing co-first authorship and now in our final year of university, began this project back in 2024, and it is incredibly rewarding to see it finally come together.

title: Glyph: An Interpretability Engine for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery in Clinical Data

details.title: Glyph: An Interpretability Engine for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery in Clinical Data
details.abstract: Can model interpretability help us learn something new about human health? Glyph is a framework for AI-accelerated clinical science. It uses sparse autoencoders to uncover patterns in multimodal clinical data hidden within foundation models, turning them into concepts researchers can investigate. This revealed known and potentially novel risk markers at scale that reproduced across hospitals and improved risk prediction beyond markers drawn from the clinical literature. More broadly, we show how interpretability could move beyond explaining models to expanding clinical knowledge. Glyph is open source, allowing researchers to extract our concept space from their own data. They can also discover new concept spaces in their own data, share their findings, and test whether those findings reproduce across datasets. We envision this facilitating reproducible clinical discovery at scale.

title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate

details.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
details.abstract: System One models such as Jev return decisions through fast, parallel prediction. In this paper, we introduce Jeveration, showing that the same decision paradigm can also generate high-quality images in a single forward pass. Jeveration builds on a frozen vision-language model, repurposing its visual-semantic knowledge for holistic image generation. The key challenge is to maintain global consistency. A single prompt admits many valid images, yet parallel predictions must converge on a coherent whole. We therefore condition all positions on a shared random state to coordinate parallel predictions, so that each draw yields a different but coherent image. Since the model tends to ignore this state under direct image supervision, we first learn a distribution over discrete image codes to guide single-pass generation. Beyond text-to-image generation, we further unify image-to-image generation and dense prediction within the same architecture, so that one checkpoint supports all three tasks, each in one forward pass. Experiments show that Jeveration generates a 512x512 image in 78 ms, up to 122x faster than existing unified models, while maintaining competitive image quality and dense prediction performance.

title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements

details.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
details.abstract: TL;DR: Much of the current community effort on agent evolution / RSI (across skills, harnesses, memory, etc.) is focusing on the wrong bottleneck. Proposing better artifacts is actually quite easy—the real challenge is reliably identifying whether an artifact truly helps. In fact, many seemingly impressive gains reported in recent work come down to exploiting evaluation shortcuts. Everything you want to know about the reality of agent evolution is in this paper. For instance, we mapped out the actual score density distributions across mainstream evolution methods, frontier models, and standard benchmarks (spanning 1,030+ evolution runs and 10M+ LLM calls!). Everyone in the field has wanted to see these curves, though computing each one is prohibitively expensive—so we bit the bullet and absorbed the cost to save the community from hitting the same walls. Surprise: Many of these score distributions aren't Gaussian at all—they are multimodal ! We also packed the paper with tons of hard-earned, practical insights: How can a single sentence hack mainstream benchmarks and reproduce 90% of full evolution gains? Are there actually transferable skills that genuinely boost performance on Terminal-Bench v2.1 ? (Spoiler: Yes, and we show why standard selectors miss them.) Plus plenty more actionable know-how inside. If you are building or evaluating self-evolving agents, you'll definitely walk away with something valuable! 🔗 Project Page: https://lineshogan.github.io/resolution-hypothesis/

title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive

details.title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
details.abstract: 🚀 From Passive Video Understanding to Proactive, Interactive AI Assistants! We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model that goes beyond simply watching and answering questions. ALIVE enables three key capabilities: 🔵  Proactive Monitoring: Continuously observe the world and respond when relevant events occur. 🟣 Streaming Task Coordination: Manage evolving user requests across multi-turn interactions. 🟠 Feedback-Seeking Interaction: Proactively ask for missing information or user actions to complete tasks. To achieve this, we introduce ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K, combining contrastive supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning using Behavior-Aligned Credit Assignment (BACA). We also introduce FSI-Bench to evaluate feedback-seeking capabilities. 🏆 ALIVE achieves the highest overall scores among compared models across four public benchmarks and FSI-Bench. A step toward AI assistants that don't just watch and answer, but proactively interact and collaborate with users!

title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling

details.title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
details.abstract: PROLA introduces Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), a new task that jointly addresses future weather prediction and spatiotemporal resolution refinement. We propose a scaffold-and-correct framework and Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation (PROLA), which allocates a fixed rank budget between principal and orthogonal weight subspaces and adaptively scales optimizer updates using gradient signals. PROLA consistently outperforms representative PEFT baselines across global and regional weather benchmarks, while requiring less than 0.4% of the trainable parameters used in full fine-tuning on the main benchmark. Additional experiments demonstrate its effectiveness across different weather tasks and pretrained backbones.

title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development

details.title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
details.abstract: Game2Player scales gameplay experience for visual agents by turning existing web games into verifiable environments. A coding player and a visual player test tasks, report problems, and collect training trajectories, yielding 568 games, 3,436 tasks, and 307 hours of gameplay. Training on these trajectories raises a 9B model’s progress from 14.3% to 31.2% on held-out PlayerBench games, with gains that transfer to GameWorld. The environment–player feedback loop improves task verification while producing data for visual agent training.

title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning

details.title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
details.abstract: CurvDelta models the weight change ΔW directly in a low-curvature subspace. Projecting each gradient can still let an optimizer like Adam move the weights outside that space. Our parameterization keeps ΔW inside it throughout training. Our low-rank variant takes the same form as LoRA methods that constrain the update space. Those methods often choose the space using heuristics based on weights or activations. We derive it from the local curvature of the preservation loss. This gives the constraint a concrete meaning: for an update, the curvature we retain bounds the predicted increase in preservation loss near the original model.

title: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning

details.title: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
details.abstract: LightTAR quickly learns task-specific text and image features for tabular models, significantly improving predictive performance over standard frozen embeddings with minimal computational overhead.

title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules

details.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
details.abstract: We present WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules, a framework for generating interactive video worlds that follow configurable rules.

title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation

details.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re sharing Invoker-Render, the video renderer behind Code World Model 2.0. It takes a structural proxy, a reference image, and a text prompt. A coarse proxy can tell the model where a character moves and let it synthesize a natural gait, while a more detailed proxy can guide individual limb movements. For streaming, we use Progressive Forcing to distill the causal renderer to four denoising steps per chunk, then train it on its own generated history to reduce drift. In our continuous 30-minute racing demo, the renderer follows the input trajectory while keeping the car and scene visually consistent. We’d love to hear what you’d try with it!

title: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model

details.title: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model
details.abstract: Interactive video world models turn user commands into the exploration of a generated scene, which requires the scene to keep its 3D structure as the camera moves and each action to keep a stable effect. Existing benchmarks mostly evaluate these properties against references fitted to the video under test, either a scene reconstructed from its own frames or a camera trajectory aligned to the command path with a free scale. Such references can absorb gradual scene deformation and changes in pace and route length, so these errors can pass undetected. We therefore introduce StrideWorld, a benchmark whose references are fixed before the motion they judge. It evaluates scene rigidity against the ground-truth geometry of the start view, and action consistency against the stride of each action, the camera motion of one command. The stride is measured on the model's first steps and then used to test the steps that follow, so each model is judged only against its own steps. Its measurements are validated on rendered videos with known camera motion, and its scores agree with human judgments. Across 54600 videos generated by 15 open models from 140 start views, all models but one deform their scenes as the camera moves, with offsets up to 7.3 times those of a rigid rendering along the same camera path. Most models keep a steady pace when a single action is held. Along composed routes, several models often stall, and most completed routes end away from the positions predicted by each model's own strides. Only the two models that scale commands by the estimated scene depth bring most routes close to these positions. Fine-tuning two models on a few rendered clips removes most of their mid-route stalls. Code, data, and a leaderboard are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/spaces/strideworld-release/strideworld-leaderboard .

title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models

details.title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
details.abstract: Accepted to KDD 2027 We introduce RoughCut-Bench , a benchmark for automatic video rough-cut with large vision-language models. It covers two practical settings: visually driven editing—highlight selection, source-media ordering, and optional user requirements—and speech-driven cleanup of ASR transcripts. The benchmark includes 101 visual cases , 831 source assets , and 1,476 highlight annotations , plus 84 speech-driven cases . We provide agentic workflows that generate executable cut plans, together with annotation-based metrics and a human-aligned agentic evaluator for rendered cuts. Our experiments highlight the remaining gap between current LVLMs and expert editing decisions. Code, prompts, and benchmark data are publicly available.
